name: Desiccated organ supplements (beef organs capsules)

card.summary: Freeze-dried beef liver and organ capsules marketed as a convenient 'nature's multivitamin', with no appearance trials behind them.
card.aka: Beef organ capsules, freeze-dried liver, organ complex, desiccated liver
card.note: Liver-based products supply preformed vitamin A, for which an upper intake level exists; supplements are not regulated like drugs.

quick.overview:
Desiccated organ supplements are capsules or powders made from dried beef liver and sometimes other organs such as heart, kidney or spleen. They are sold as a way to get the nutrients of organ meats without cooking or tasting them, and are popular in ancestral-diet and looksmaxxing circles.

The underlying idea is that organ meats are nutrient-dense, which reference sources confirm for liver. No published trial was found testing these capsules for skin, hair, energy or appearance.
quick.mechanism: The capsules deliver the nutrients found in the source organ, mainly in liver preformed vitamin A, B12, riboflavin, iron and copper. Proponents say this supports skin and vitality; this has not been tested for the capsule products themselves.
quick.risks: Liver-derived products contain preformed vitamin A, for which health sources list a tolerable upper intake level of 3,000 micrograms per day for adults and advise limits in pregnancy. Dietary supplements are not approved as drugs, and content and quality vary by manufacturer.

lead: Desiccated organ supplements, often sold as beef organ capsules, are dried and encapsulated preparations of animal organs, most commonly beef liver, sometimes combined with heart, kidney, spleen or other tissue. They are promoted in ancestral-diet communities as a convenient substitute for eating organ meats.

Liver, the main ingredient, is documented as a very rich source of preformed vitamin A, vitamin B12, riboflavin, iron and copper [1]. Reference sources also document that excess preformed vitamin A can cause toxicity, including liver damage, bone effects and harm in pregnancy [2].

No published human study was found testing organ capsules for skin, appearance or general health outcomes, so claims about their benefits rest on the nutrient profile of the source organs and on user reports.
infobox: Dried animal organs, usually beef liver

Sold as dietary supplements, not approved drugs

paras: These products are made by drying, usually by freeze-drying, animal organs and packing the powder into capsules or selling it loose. They are one way of obtaining organ meat nutrients that does not require cooking or eating the food itself. Offal has been eaten across many cuisines for centuries [3].

Fresh liver is a concentrated source of vitamin A, B12, riboflavin and iron, and its vitamin A content is high enough that one slice of beef liver can exceed the adult upper intake level [1]. Because liver-based capsules concentrate the same organ, products derived from it supply preformed vitamin A, whose excess is associated with headache, skin and hair effects, liver damage, bone resorption and birth defects [2]. The upper intake level for adults is listed at 3,000 micrograms per day, and possible pregnancy calls for limits on vitamin A [2].
Dietary supplements are not reviewed as drugs, and the amount of any nutrient in a given product varies with manufacturer and batch.

No studies found. No published human trial has tested desiccated organ or liver capsules for appearance, skin or general health. Studies of the nutrient content of liver as a food exist in reference sources [1], but they do not test the capsule products.
